title: Detect Missing or Duplicate Keys in Children
problemStatement: Implement `validateKeys(children)` that inspects an array of child objects `{ key, type }` and returns `{ valid: boolean, duplicateKeys: string[], missingCount: number }`.
interviewTrap: Keys must be unique strictly among SIBLINGS, not across the entire application.

testCases.name: Validates list with unique stable keys
testCases.testFn: const res = validateKeys([{ key: 'a' }, { key: 'b' }, { key: 'c' }]); return { valid: res.valid, missingCount: res.missingCount, duplicateCount: res.duplicateKeys.length };

testCases.name: Detects duplicate keys in sibling list
testCases.testFn: const res = validateKeys([{ key: 'item-1' }, { key: 'item-2' }, { key: 'item-1' }]); return res.duplicateKeys;

testCases.name: Counts children with missing keys
testCases.testFn: const res = validateKeys([{ key: 'x' }, {}, { type: 'div' }]); return res.missingCount;

details.name: Validates list with unique stable keys
Detects duplicate keys in sibling list

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React's list reconciliation algorithm requires unique, stable `key` props on array children to identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed. Missing keys or duplicate keys trigger console warnings and cause severe DOM diffing bugs.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Accept an array of React element children.
Initialize `seenKeys = new Set()` and diagnostic result object `{ missingCount: 0, duplicates: [] }`.
- If child has no `key` property (or `key === null` or `key === undefined`), increment `missingCount++`.
- If child has a key, check if `seenKeys.has(child.key)`: if already seen, push `child.key` to `duplicates`; else `seenKeys.add(child.key)`.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In `packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactChildFiber.js`, `reconcileChildrenArray` checks keys. If a key is missing, React warns in development. If keys are duplicated, React logs a warning and cannot guarantee which child will retain state or receive DOM updates.

complexity.time: O(N) single linear scan over children array.
complexity.space: O(N) Set storage for distinct keys.

edgeCasesHandled: All unique keys report 0 missing and 0 duplicates.
Multiple duplicates of the same key captured without crashing.

specifications: React Official Docs: Preserving and Resetting State (Rules of Keys)
verifiedRules: Keys must be unique among siblings.
Missing keys disable optimal child matching and force linear fallback diffing.
